headline: When to Call a Professional for Kitchen Cabinet Tear-Out
articleBody:
Tearing out old kitchen cabinets sounds like an easy weekend project, but it often escalates the minute you encounter stubborn adhesive, gas appliances, or hidden wiring. Knowing when to step back and call a professional saves money on drywall and pipe repairs down the road.

Common Mistakes to Avoid
- Tugging on Cabinets Connected to Live Utilities: Old under-cabinet lights, hardwired garbage disposals, and adjacent gas ranges require careful isolation. Cutting wires blindly or bumping gas connections creates immediate hazards.
- Prying Against Drywall Without Finding Stud Screws: Ripping cabinets straight off the wall tears the drywall facing paper down to the studs, turning a simple cabinet swap into a major drywall patching job.
- Failing to Support Heavy Upper Boxes: Upper cabinets are heavy. Backing out screws without a partner or support brace can cause the cabinet to drop, cracking counters or injuring hands.
- Ignoring Age of the Home: If your home was built before 1978, disturbing painted finishes can release lead dust, which requires EPA lead-safe containment techniques.

When Professional Guidance Helps
If your cabinet removal involves heavy stone countertops, built-in appliances, concealed plumbing drops, or subfloor modifications, having a general contractor handle the work keeps the area safe and structurally sound.
